hints: Focus on the C=C double bond in propene and see whether atoms are being added across it or removed from it in reaction 1.
In reaction 1, H and I from HI both join the carbon skeleton to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CHICH}_3$, so think about which reaction type adds across a double bond.
In reaction 2, compare $\text{CH}_3\text{CHICH}_3$ with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ and notice that I is swapped for OH with everything else unchanged.
walkthrough:
**Look at reaction 1**

Think of addition as two pieces joining together across a double bond. Here the double bond disappears.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{HI} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHICH}_3$$

**Check the atom count**

Two reactant molecules combine to make one larger product molecule. H adds to one carbon and I adds to the other. That is electrophilic addition to an alkene.

**Look at reaction 2**

Think of substitution as a swap. The carbon skeleton stays the same, but one group leaves and another takes its place.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHICH}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 + \text{I}^-$$

**Conclude the pair**

I is replaced by OH to form the alcohol. That is nucleophilic substitution of a halogenoalkane. So we have addition followed by substitution.

options.A: Reaction 1 is correctly addition, but reaction 2 is not elimination. Elimination would remove HI or H2O and reform a C=C double bond, but here the product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ is still saturated.
options.B: Reaction 1 is addition because HI adds across the C=C of propene to give 2-iodopropane. Reaction 2 is substitution because I in $\text{CH}_3\text{CHICH}_3$ is swapped for OH from KOH to give propan-2-ol.
options.C: Reaction 2 is correctly substitution, but reaction 1 is not elimination. Elimination decreases the number of atoms and forms a double bond, while here atoms are gained and the double bond is lost.
options.D: Both labels are reversed. Reaction 1 cannot be substitution because there is no group to swap on the alkene, the double bond is attacked instead. Reaction 2 cannot be elimination because no alkene is formed.
